title: Where a guarded command runs
text: Write guards and the workspace-cwd writer guard resolve a relative path in the directory of the segment it appears in: the command's declared workdir, moved by every plain `cd` before that segment, including a `cd` after an earlier command. A `cd` to a variable, a backtick or `cd -` leaves later directories unknown. Codex carries the workdir only in its local rollout; the hook client stamps it, matching a code-mode call by its exact command when the hook id is the inner item id. The client's own path answer is used only when it names the same path, so a client that missed the directory cannot move a lane write onto main. Observed in source and tests; deployed harness proof is pending. Direct exec_command rollout arguments and the input payload container carry the same workdir authority. Python temporary-directory/file factories and computed scratch prefixes avoid a false cwd target; explicit source writes and unresolved non-scratch writes retain checks. Registered checkout and lane boundaries take precedence over scratch-root inference, including checkouts stored in temporary directories.
